_meta.description: budget-core-schema — the data foundation for begroting (budgeting): LedgerGroup (verzamelpost, REQ-BCS-004/005), AnnualBudget (the fiscal-year budget container + one-default invariant, REQ-BCS-006), and BudgetLine (AnnualBudget x LedgerGroup crossed with 12 monthly phased amounts + a source marker, REQ-BCS-007). Seeded from lib/Settings/statements/rj270-pl.json (P&L-shaped, not the balance sheet — a begroting is a monthly-phased flow plan, design.md §3c). The budget-vs-actuals roll-up is a PHP service (BudgetVsActualsReader/Calculator), not a declarative aggregation — see design.md §6.

LedgerGroup.title: Ledger Group
LedgerGroup.description: A per-administration, ordered, nestable grouping of GL accounts (verzamelpost) — the reusable grouping unit both the RJ270 statement manifests and the begroting grid need. Members are resolved at evaluation time from an optional accountRanges array plus explicit includedAccountNumbers/excludedAccountNumbers — never a declarative filter (design.md §3a). No lifecycle: a LedgerGroup is configuration, edited directly, consistent with Account/AllocationRule/the rubriek-mapping precedent.

administrationId.description: FK to the Administration owning this ledger group. Every reviewed schema in this codebase denormalises this directly, even under a parent FK (design.md §3b).
administrationId.title: Administration ID

code.description: Short operator-facing identifier for this group.
code.title: Code

order.description: Sibling ordering within the same parent (or among roots when parentLedgerGroupId is null).
order.title: Order

parentLedgerGroupId.description: Self-FK holding the parent LedgerGroup's `code` — a flat business key, exactly as the description says it mirrors: Account.parentAccountNumber references an accountNumber, not an object id. Null for a root group. WHY A BUSINESS KEY AND NOT AN ID: a real object id is not known at seed-authoring time, and OpenRegister's `@ref:` seed-token mechanism (which would mint one) is unusable here — it only walks `components.objects`, a bucket shillinq's fragment merge currently corrupts (see _objects_placement_note). A `code` is the only parent identity BOTH the PHP rollup and the manifest's declarative filter engine can resolve: the LedgerGroupDetail `children` relatedCollection filters `parentLedgerGroupId == @object.code`, and `@object.<field>` reads a FLAT payload field only — it cannot reach `@self.slug`. `code` is unique within an administration, which is the scope BudgetVsActualsReader loads. BudgetVsActualsReader keeps its id|slug|code lookup so hand-authored id or slug references still resolve. A parent with children uses its OWN BudgetLine if one exists; otherwise its value is the recursive sum of its children's resolved values (design.md §3d) — no double counting when both exist.
parentLedgerGroupId.title: Parent Ledger Group Code

accountRanges.description: Inclusive numeric-string account-number range pairs (RJ270 array-pair convention, not the rubriek-mapping hyphenated string). Default membership before includedAccountNumbers/excludedAccountNumbers are applied (design.md §3a). A group with none of the three (accountRanges/includedAccountNumbers/excludedAccountNumbers) has no members — a valid, if useless, state the schema does not forbid.
accountRanges.title: Account Ranges

includedAccountNumbers.description: Explicit account-number adds, regardless of accountRanges — the escape hatch for a chart of accounts that does not align perfectly to RGS ranges.
includedAccountNumbers.title: Included Account Numbers

excludedAccountNumbers.description: Explicit carve-outs from any matching accountRanges entry.
excludedAccountNumbers.title: Excluded Account Numbers

effectiveFrom.description: Date from which this group applies (ISO-8601), per the ChartOfAccountsMapping precedent.
effectiveFrom.title: Effective From

effectiveTo.description: Date this group ceases to apply; null while open-ended.
effectiveTo.title: Effective To

x-openregister-audit-trail.description: Every create, update and delete of a LedgerGroup is written to OpenRegister's immutable audit trail with actor and timestamp.

AnnualBudget.title: Annual Budget
AnnualBudget.description: The fiscal-year budget container (begroting), crossed with LedgerGroup via BudgetLine. Carries the one-default invariant AnnualBudgetDefaultGuard enforces on the activate transition: at most one AnnualBudget per administrationId + fiscalYear may have isDefault=true — aligned now so the budget-scenarios follow-up change does not need to retrofit it (design.md §4b).

administrationId.description: FK to the Administration owning this budget.
administrationId.title: Administration ID

fiscalYear.description: Fiscal year this budget applies to.
fiscalYear.title: Fiscal Year

isDefault.description: Whether this is the default AnnualBudget for its administrationId + fiscalYear. Governs WHICH ONE WINS when more than one active budget could theoretically exist for the same year (e.g. a draft alternate/scenario budget under budget-scenarios) — a separate axis from state, which governs editability (design.md §4b).
isDefault.title: Is Default

state.description: Lifecycle state. draft: under construction, lines editable. active: the budget in force for its fiscal year, lines still editable. closed: locked at year-end, superseded, retained for audit.
state.title: State

active.label: Active
active.description: The budget in force for its fiscal year; lines still editable.

closed.label: Closed
closed.description: Locked at year-end; superseded, retained for audit.

activate.label: Activate budget
activate.description: Requires no other AnnualBudget with isDefault=true for the same administrationId+fiscalYear.

close.label: Close budget
close.description: Year-end lock; no further line edits.

x-openregister-audit-trail.description: Every create, update and delete of an AnnualBudget is written to OpenRegister's immutable audit trail with actor and timestamp.

BudgetLine.title: Budget Line
BudgetLine.description: AnnualBudget x LedgerGroup crossed with 12 monthly phased amounts and a source marker — the spreadsheet mental model's row. This change writes only source=manual lines (an operator typing a number); contract/recurring/projected/scenario are declared for budget-known-costs, budget-projection-engine and budget-scenarios to populate later. The cumulative 13th-column total is a UI concern (budget-grid-view), not a stored field, per design.md §5b.

administrationId.description: FK to the Administration owning this budget line.
administrationId.title: Administration ID

ledgerGroupId.description: FK to the LedgerGroup this line phases amounts against.

source.description: How this line's amounts were populated. manual: operator-entered (this change's only writer). contract/recurring: budget-known-costs. projected: budget-projection-engine. scenario: budget-scenarios.

budgetVsActuals.description: DOCUMENTATION-ONLY declarative shape for the budget-vs-actuals roll-up. This is NOT the computed path this change depends on — BudgetVsActualsReader/BudgetVsActualsCalculator (PHP) is the primary, PHPUnit-tested path, because AggregationAnnotationValidator validates cross-schema filter fields against the DECLARING schema's own properties rather than the TARGET schema's, silently discarding the annotation on a mismatch (design.md §6a). UNVERIFIED / EXPECTED-DISCARDED pending the positive-control task (grep nextcloud.log for "annotation on schema" after a fresh import) — do not wire any page to depend on this block.

_objects_placement_note: These seed objects sit at the TOP-LEVEL `objects` key, NOT under `components.objects`. Both buckets are imported by OpenRegister's ImportHandler, but SettingsService::deepMergeConfig() currently mis-merges the `components.objects` bucket across fragments: measured on this tree it keeps only 98 of the ~483 objects the fragments declare, later fragments overwriting earlier ones index-by-index. Moving these 19 rows there loses 11 of them AND clobbers 19 rows belonging to other fragments. Do not move them until that merge bug is fixed (tracked separately). CONSEQUENCE: `@ref:<schema>:<slug>` seed-reference tokens — which the importer rewrites into the target object's UUID — are NOT usable here, because resolveSeedReferenceTokens() only walks `components.objects`. That is why parentLedgerGroupId below carries the parent's `code` (a flat business key, exactly like Account.parentAccountNumber) rather than an object id: it is the only parent identity that both the PHP rollup and the manifest's `@object.code` filter token can resolve. SECOND TRAP: the import loop only re-saves an ALREADY-IMPORTED object when the incoming `@self.version` compares HIGHER than the stored one (both default to '1.0.0'), so on any instance that already seeded these rows an edit here is a silent no-op — the old values stay in the database and nothing is logged at warning level. The eight child rows therefore carry `@self.version: "1.0.1"`; bump it again on any future change to their payload.
